Get ready to head out of the city, visit new areas and embrace the quieter side of Japan whilst game hunting to find the best deals. Making sure you have mobile data as soon as you arrive is going to make or break your trip, so I've teamed up with @airalo_apac (ad) to give you an exclusive discount on their eSIM plans. transcription: After living in Japan for three years, I think it's about time that I shared my top three tips for retro game shopping. Number one is prepare to head out of the city to find the best deals. Central Tokyo, Akihabara and Denben Town are all crazy busy right now and the prices are going to reflect that. But if you head further out into the suburbs, even into Chiba, you're much more likely to find something cool, like those box-gracation ones that I picked up for a hundred yen in Kamioca on the outskirts of Kyoto. My second tip is to make sure that you have mobile data for the the full duration of your trip. This is going to help massively with comparing prices, finding the stores you want to visit and getting to them via public transport. My recommendation is to grab an Eastern from AeroLo and skip the pickup lines for some cars at the airport. They have a range of affordable plans that give you flexible data usage, but the option to top up whenever you need to. You'll get an instant internet connection as soon as you land in Japan so you can get straight into the junk section and see what's on offer. AeroLo Eastings are actually available in over 200 countries and regions worldwide, and You can save $3 by using Code Retro Game and signing up with Billink in my bio. Tip number three is to shop tax-free. If you're visiting from overseas, look out for these signs whilst on your travels and present your passport to make the most of tax-free shopping. You'll need to be spending more than $5,000 in yen, but that's pretty easy when the stores have shelves that look like this.
